youtube_title: Rogers City, Michigan: the Carl D. Bradley, the night 33 men were lost (1958)
youtube:
You asked for Rogers City! In one night, 33 men were lost, and 23 of them were from Rogers City, Michigan. In November 1958 the limestone freighter Carl D. Bradley, more than 600 feet long, left Gary, Indiana, empty, bound for Calcite at Rogers City. On Lake Michigan the next day, winds topped 60 miles an hour and waves were about 25 feet high. Around 5:30 that evening she broke in two. A Mayday went out just as the power failed. Of 35 men aboard, 2 survived on a raft through the night. More than 50 children in Rogers City lost their fathers. Today a sailors' memorial by the lake in Rogers City lists the crew's names. Comment your town for the next LaPorte After Dark! #RogersCity #Michigan #CarlDBradley #Shipwreck #GreatLakes #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn; no one is shown in the water, and the anchor drawn is not the Bradley's. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: U.S. Coast Guard Marine Board of Investigation and Commandant's Action (1959); Rogers City Sailors Memorial marker; Wisconsin Marine Historical Society; WCMU (2025); Presque Isle County Advance; NOAA Mariners Weather Log (2004); The Alpena News.
